blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Chapter 3 (Circular and Rotational Motion), arranged by the chapter's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each answer is a short model answer; small numericals show the working, and a comparison is answered as a table.

blocks.prompt: 1 Define one radian.
blocks.explanation: If the length of an arc AB of a circle is equal to the radius r of the circle, the angle it makes at the centre O is called one radian. It is the SI unit of angular measurement; its symbol is rad.

book_ref.quote: then the angle is called one radian

blocks.prompt: 2 A body moves in a circle with constant speed. Why is its velocity not constant?
blocks.explanation: In a circular path the direction of motion changes continuously. Velocity is a vector, so a change of direction alone means the velocity changes, even though the speed is constant.

book_ref.quote: this change of direction means that their velocities are not constant

blocks.prompt: 3 What is angular displacement? When is it treated as a vector?
blocks.explanation: The angle Δθ through which the line OP turns in a time interval Δt is its angular displacement. It is positive for counter clockwise rotation. Only for very small values of Δθ is angular displacement a vector, directed along the axis of rotation.

book_ref.quote: defines the angular displacement of OP during the time interval

blocks.prompt: 4 State the right hand rule for the direction of angular displacement.
blocks.explanation: Grasp the axis of rotation in the right hand with the fingers curling in the direction of rotation; the thumb then points in the direction of the angular displacement (along the axis).

book_ref.quote: Grasp the axis of rotation in right hand with fingers curling in the direction of rotation

blocks.prompt: 5 Name the units of angular displacement and give the relations between them.
blocks.explanation:
Degree, revolution and radian.
1 revolution = 2π rad = 360°
1 rad = 360°/2π = 57.3°

book_ref.quote: Three units are generally used to express angular displacement

blocks.prompt: 6 Express an angle of 450° in radians and in revolutions.
blocks.explanation:
In radian: 450° × (2π rad/360°) = 2.5π rad = 7.85 rad
In revolutions: 450°/360° = 1.25 rev

book_ref.quote: Consider an arc of length S of a circle of radius r

blocks.prompt: 7 Define angular velocity. Give its SI unit and direction.
blocks.explanation: Angular velocity is the rate at which the angular displacement changes with time: ω_av = Δθ/Δt; instantaneous ω is the limit of Δθ/Δt as Δt → 0. SI unit: rad s⁻¹ (also rpm is used). Direction: along the axis of rotation by the right hand rule.

book_ref.quote: defined as the rate at which the angular displacement is changing with time

blocks.prompt: 8 A grinding wheel rotates at 900 rpm. Find its angular velocity in rad s⁻¹.
blocks.explanation:
900 rev/min = 900/60 = 15 rev s⁻¹
ω = 15 × 2π = 30π rad s⁻¹ = 94.2 rad s⁻¹

book_ref.quote: Sometimes it is also given in terms of revolution per minute (rpm).

blocks.prompt: 9 Define angular acceleration. Give its unit and direction.
blocks.explanation: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity: α_av = (ω_f − ωᵢ)/(t_f − tᵢ) = Δω/Δt; instantaneous α is the limit as Δt → 0. Unit: rad s⁻². It is a vector directed along the axis of rotation.

book_ref.quote: We define angular acceleration as the rate of change of angular velocity.

blocks.prompt: 10 What is the reference line of a rotating rigid body? Why is it useful?
blocks.explanation: The perpendicular OP dropped from a point P of the body on the axis of rotation is the reference line. It rotates with the same angular velocity and angular acceleration as the body, so the rotation of the whole rigid body can be described by the rotation of OP.

book_ref.quote: usually referred as the reference line

blocks.prompt: 11 Why is the linear velocity of a point on a rotating body called tangential velocity?
blocks.explanation: As Δt → 0 the arc P₁P₂ becomes very small and its direction is that of the tangent to the circle at P₁. So the velocity of P always points along the tangent to the circle at that point, hence the name tangential velocity.

book_ref.quote: the linear velocity of the point P is also known as tangential velocity

blocks.prompt: 12 Differentiate between linear (tangential) velocity and angular velocity.
blocks.explanation: Linear velocity describes how fast a point moves along the circle; angular velocity describes how fast the reference line turns.

book_ref.quote: We are interested in finding out the relation between ω and v.

rows: Rate of change of distance along the circle (ΔS/Δt).
Rate of change of angular displacement (Δθ/Δt).
Directed along the tangent to the circle.
Directed along the axis of rotation.
Different for points at different distances from the axis.
Same for all points of a rigid body.

blocks.prompt: 13 A wheel of radius 0.35 m rotates at 12 rad s⁻¹. Find the linear speed of a point on its rim.
blocks.explanation: v = rω = 0.35 m × 12 rad s⁻¹ = 4.2 m s⁻¹

book_ref.quote: Imagine a point P in the rigid body at a perpendicular distance r from the axis of rotation.

blocks.prompt: 14 On a rotating rigid body, which quantities are the same for all points and which are not? Why?
blocks.explanation: Angular displacement, angular speed and angular acceleration are the same for all points at any instant. Linear speed v = rω and tangential acceleration aₜ = rα depend on r, so points at different distances from the axis have different values.

book_ref.quote: points that are at different distances from the axis do not have the same speed or acceleration

blocks.prompt: 15 Write the equations of angular motion with their linear counterparts.
blocks.explanation: Replace S, v and a by θ, ω and α:

book_ref.quote: Given below are angular equations together with their linear counterparts.

blocks.prompt: 16 Under what condition do the equations of angular motion hold? Why?
blocks.explanation: They hold only when the axis of rotation is fixed. Then all angular vectors (θ, ω, α) have the same direction along the axis, so they can be manipulated as scalars.

book_ref.quote: hold true only in the case when the axis of rotation is fixed, so that all the angular vectors have the same direction

blocks.prompt: 17 A wheel starts from rest with a uniform angular acceleration of 4.0 rad s⁻². Find its angular velocity and the angle turned after 5.0 s.
blocks.explanation:
ω_f = ωᵢ + αt = 0 + 4.0 × 5.0 = 20 rad s⁻¹
θ = ωᵢt + ½αt² = 0 + ½ × 4.0 × 5.0² = 50 rad

book_ref.quote: Assuming deceleration to be uniform, find its value.

blocks.prompt: 18 Define centripetal force and write its formula.
blocks.explanation: The force needed to bend the straight path of a particle into a circular path is the centripetal (centre seeking) force. It acts along the radius towards the centre: F꜀ = mv²/r = mrω².

book_ref.quote: The force needed to bend the straight path of the particle into a circular path is called the centripetal force.

blocks.prompt: 19 Why does the centripetal force not change the speed of a body moving in a circle?
blocks.explanation: The centripetal force acts along the radius, perpendicular to the tangential velocity at each point. A force perpendicular to the velocity changes only the direction of motion, so the speed stays the same.

book_ref.quote: The force that does not alter speed but only direction at each point is a perpendicular force

blocks.prompt: 20 A ball whirled on a string moves off along a tangent when the string snaps. Why?
blocks.explanation: The tension in the string was the centripetal force bending the path into a circle. When the string snaps at A, no centripetal force acts, so the ball continues with its velocity at A, which is along the tangent AB.

book_ref.quote: the ball will follow the straight line path AB which is tangent AB at point A

blocks.prompt: 21 Differentiate between the effect of a force acting along the velocity of a moving body and a force acting perpendicular to it.
blocks.explanation: A force along the velocity changes the speed; a perpendicular force changes only the direction.

book_ref.quote: A force acting on a moving body along the direction of its velocity will change magnitude of the velocity (speed) keeping the direction unchanged.

rows: Body moves in a straight line.
Body moves in a circle (centripetal force).

blocks.prompt: 22 Show that the centripetal force can be written as F꜀ = mrω².
blocks.explanation:
F꜀ = mv²/r. Putting v = rω:
F꜀ = m(rω)²/r = mr²ω²/r = mrω²

book_ref.quote: As v = rω, so the above equation becomes:

blocks.prompt: 23 A 1.5 kg ball moves at 3.0 m s⁻¹ in a horizontal circle of radius 2.0 m. Find the centripetal force on it.

book_ref.quote: For a body of mass m moving with velocity v in a circular path of radius r

blocks.prompt: 24 A record of diameter 30 cm turns at 45 rpm. Find the radial acceleration of a point on its rim.

book_ref.quote: what is the radial acceleration of a point on the outer rim of the CD

blocks.prompt: 25 Write the tension in the string at the top of a vertical circle. When does it become zero?
blocks.explanation: At the top, tension T and weight mg both act towards the centre and together give the centripetal force: T + mg = mv²/r, so T = m(v²/r − g). T becomes zero when v²/r = g; then the weight alone provides the centripetal force.

book_ref.quote: two forces act on the ball, the pull of the string and the weight w of the ball

blocks.prompt: 26 Why does water not fall out of a bucket whirled rapidly in a vertical circle, even at the top?
blocks.explanation: At the top, the water needs a centripetal force mv²/r towards the centre. When the bucket moves fast, mv²/r is greater than (or equal to) the weight mg, so the weight together with the push of the bucket is just used up in keeping the water moving on the circle; nothing is left to pull it out of the bucket.

book_ref.quote: When a bucket full of water is rapidly whirled in a vertical circular path

blocks.prompt: 27 What provides the centripetal force (i) for an object placed on a rotating turntable (ii) for a charged particle in a perpendicular magnetic field?
blocks.explanation:
(i) The friction between the object and the turntable.
(ii) The normal (perpendicular) magnetic force, which bends the straight path of the charged particle into a circle.

book_ref.quote: In every circular or orbital motion, centripetal force is needed which is provided by some agency.

blocks.prompt: 28 Why are highway roads banked at turns?
blocks.explanation: On a level road the centripetal force for a turn comes from friction between tyres and road. On a slippery road at high speed friction may not be enough, and the vehicle may skid or topple. So the outer edge is kept slightly higher than the inner edge, because friction alone cannot provide the necessary centripetal force.

book_ref.quote: To overcome this difficulty, the highway road is banked on turns.

blocks.prompt: 29 A 1200 kg car takes a turn of radius 80 m at 20 m s⁻¹ on a level road. How much friction must the road provide?
blocks.explanation:
Friction provides the centripetal force:
F = mv²/r = 1200 × 20² / 80 = 6000 N

book_ref.quote: which is provided by the friction between the tyres and the road

blocks.prompt: 30 What is a centrifuge? State its principle.
blocks.explanation: A centrifuge is a laboratory device that separates denser and lighter particles from a mixture by rotating it at high speed. Principle: if the force on a particle falls short of the required centripetal force, it moves away from the centre; denser particles settle at the bottom of the tubes and lighter ones rise to the top.

book_ref.quote: The centrifuge (Fig. 3.8-a) functions on this basic principle.

blocks.prompt: 31 How does the dryer of a washing machine dry the clothes?
blocks.explanation: Wet clothes are put in a long cylinder with hundreds of small holes in its wall and the cylinder is rotated rapidly. The force on the water is not enough to keep it moving in the circle, so water moves outward to the walls and drains through the holes.

book_ref.quote: The dryer consists of a long cylinder with hundreds of small holes on its wall.

blocks.prompt: 32 What are artificial satellites? What keeps them in their orbits?
blocks.explanation: Satellites are objects that orbit in a nearly circular path around the Earth. They are put into orbit by rockets and held there by the gravitational pull of the Earth, which supplies the centripetal acceleration v²/r.

book_ref.quote: Satellites are objects that orbit in nearly circular path around the Earth.

blocks.prompt: 33 What is critical velocity? Write its expression.
blocks.explanation: Critical velocity is the minimum velocity necessary to put a satellite into orbit (close to the Earth). From g = v²/R, v = √(gR); with g = 9.8 m s⁻² and R = 6.4 × 10⁶ m, v = 7.9 km s⁻¹.

book_ref.quote: This is the minimum velocity necessary to put a satellite into the orbit, called the critical velocity.

blocks.prompt: 34 A satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 6.67 × 10⁶ m where the gravitational acceleration is 9.0 m s⁻². Find its orbital speed.
blocks.explanation:
Gravity supplies the centripetal acceleration: g = v²/r
v = √(gr) = √(9.0 × 6.67 × 10⁶) = 7.75 × 10³ m s⁻¹ = 7.75 km s⁻¹

book_ref.quote: In a circular orbit around the Earth, the centripetal acceleration is supplied by gravity and we have

blocks.prompt: 35 Compare a satellite orbiting close to the Earth with one orbiting at a height much greater than the Earth's radius.
blocks.explanation: Gravity weakens with distance, so the higher satellite moves slower and takes longer.

book_ref.quote: The higher the satellite, the slower will be the required speed and longer it will take to complete one revolution around the Earth.

rows: Acceleration towards the Earth's centre about 9.8 m s⁻².
Acceleration smaller (decreases inversely as the square of distance from the centre).
Needs the critical velocity, about 7.9 km s⁻¹.

blocks.prompt: 36 Show that the orbital speed of a satellite does not depend on its mass.
blocks.explanation:
Gravitational force = required centripetal force:
GmₛM/r² = mₛv²/r
The satellite's mass mₛ cancels: v = √(GM/r). So any satellite at distance r has the same orbital speed whatever its mass.

book_ref.quote: This shows that the mass of the satellite is unimportant in describing the satellite's orbit.

blocks.prompt: 37 Find the orbital speed of a satellite at a height of 3600 km above the Earth's surface. (G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻², M = 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg, R = 6400 km)

book_ref.quote: Equating the gravitational force to the required centripetal force, we have

blocks.prompt: 38 What happens if a satellite at distance r from the Earth's centre has a speed less than √(GM/r)?
blocks.explanation: At distance r the satellite must have the orbital speed v = √(GM/r). Any smaller speed cannot keep it in that circular orbit; it comes tumbling back to the Earth.

book_ref.quote: Any speed less than this will bring the satellite tumbling back to the Earth.

blocks.prompt: 39 Show that a spring balance inside an orbiting satellite reads zero.
blocks.explanation: For mass m on the balance: mv²/r = mg − F_N (Eq. 3.16-a). For the satellite itself gravity gives the centripetal force: Mg = Mv²/r, so g = v²/r. Then mg = mg − F_N, so F_N = 0; the balance reads zero.

book_ref.quote: This shows that the supporting force which is acting on a body inside the satellite is zero.

blocks.prompt: 40 Why is the weightlessness in a satellite called apparent?
blocks.explanation: The Earth's gravitational force still acts on the bodies and supplies the centripetal force for the orbit; what becomes zero is only the supporting (normal) force. The satellite and everything in it fall freely together towards the Earth's centre, so the weightlessness is only apparent.

book_ref.quote: the bodies as well as the astronauts in a satellite find themselves in a state of apparent weightlessness

blocks.prompt: 41 Why is artificial gravity needed in a spacecraft, and how is it produced?
blocks.explanation: Over an extended stay, weightlessness may affect the performance of astronauts. The spaceship is set rotating about its own axis; the floor (outer rim) pushes on the astronaut and provides the centripetal force, so he presses on the floor as on the Earth.

book_ref.quote: the weightlessness may affect the performance of the astronauts present in that spacecraft

blocks.prompt: 42 A spaceship of radius 200 m must provide Earth-like gravity (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). Find its frequency of rotation and period.

book_ref.quote: When the spaceship rotates with this frequency, the artificial gravity like the Earth is provided to the inhabitants of the spaceship.

blocks.prompt: 43 A space station of radius 30 m completes one rotation in 15 s. Find the centripetal acceleration at its outer rim.
blocks.explanation:
a꜀ = R(4π²/t²) = 30 × 4π² / 15² = 5.26 m s⁻² ≈ 5.3 m s⁻²
(This is a centripetal acceleration; the angular acceleration is zero at steady ω.)

book_ref.quote: is the centripetal acceleration of a point on the outer rim, not an angular acceleration

blocks.prompt: 44 Define moment of inertia. Write its expression for a rigid body.
blocks.explanation: For a particle of mass m at distance r from the axis, the quantity mr² is its moment of inertia I. For a rigid body made of masses m₁, m₂, ... at distances r₁, r₂, ...: I = Σmᵢrᵢ² (Eq. 3.19). Unit: kg m².

book_ref.quote: The quantity mr² is known as the moment of inertia and is represented by I.

blocks.prompt: 45 Two cylinders have equal mass. Which has the greater rotational inertia, and why?
blocks.explanation: The one with the larger diameter. Moment of inertia depends not only on mass but also on r²; in the wider cylinder the mass is farther from the axis, so Σmᵢrᵢ² is larger.

book_ref.quote: Two cylinders of equal mass. The one with the larger diameter

blocks.prompt: 46 Compare Newton's second law for linear motion with its rotational analogue.
blocks.explanation: In τ = Iα, F is replaced by τ, a by α and m by I = mr².

book_ref.quote: Here F is replaced by τ, a by α and m by mr².

blocks.prompt: 47 Three small masses 0.50 kg, 0.50 kg and 1.0 kg are fixed on a light rod at 0.10 m, 0.20 m and 0.30 m from the axis. Find the moment of inertia.

book_ref.quote: Most rigid bodies have different mass concentration at different distances from the axis of rotation

blocks.prompt: 48 A wheel of moment of inertia 2.5 kg m² is brought from rest to 20 rad s⁻¹ uniformly in 4.0 s. Find the torque applied.

book_ref.quote: where I is the moment of inertia of the body and is expressed as

blocks.prompt: 49 Define angular momentum. Give its magnitude and SI unit.
blocks.explanation: The angular momentum of a particle of momentum p about origin O is L = r × p, where r is its position vector from O. Magnitude: L = rp sin θ = mrv sin θ. SI unit: kg m² s⁻¹ or J s.

book_ref.quote: relative to the origin O is defined as:

blocks.prompt: 50 How is the direction of angular momentum found?
blocks.explanation: L = r × p is perpendicular to the plane formed by r and p; its sense is given by the right hand rule of vector product. For a rotating body L is along the axis of rotation, in the direction of ω.

book_ref.quote: The direction of L is perpendicular to the plane formed by r and p

blocks.prompt: 51 Show that the angular momentum of a particle moving in a circle is L = mr²ω.
blocks.explanation: In a circle r and the tangential velocity are at 90°, so L = mrv sin 90° = mrv. Putting v = rω: L = mr(rω) = mr²ω.

book_ref.quote: then angle between r and tangential velocity is 90

blocks.prompt: 52 Differentiate between linear momentum and angular momentum.
blocks.explanation: Linear momentum belongs to translational motion; angular momentum to rotational motion.

book_ref.quote: linear momentum plays an important role in translational motion of bodies

rows: L = r × p; for a rigid body L = Iω
Direction perpendicular to r and p (along the axis).
Unit: kg m² s⁻¹ or J s.

blocks.prompt: 53 When is the angular momentum of a moving particle about a point zero?
blocks.explanation: L = rp sin θ. If the particle moves along the line through the point (θ = 0° or 180°), sin θ = 0, so L = 0 even though the particle is moving; its angular position does not change.

book_ref.quote: where θ is the angle between r and p

blocks.prompt: 54 A disc of moment of inertia 0.020 kg m² rotates at 300 rpm. Find its angular momentum.

book_ref.quote: Summing this over all particles gives the total angular momentum of the rigid body.

blocks.prompt: 55 A 1000 kg satellite moves in a circular orbit of radius 7.0 × 10⁶ m at 7.5 × 10³ m s⁻¹. Find its orbital angular momentum.

book_ref.quote: Orbital angular momentum of the Earth

blocks.text: 3.6 Law of conservation of angular momentum

blocks.prompt: 56 State the law of conservation of angular momentum.
blocks.explanation: If no external torque acts on a system, the total angular momentum of the system remains constant: L₁ + L₂ + ... = constant. For a body changing its moment of inertia: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂.

book_ref.quote: if no external torque acts on a system, the total angular momentum of the system remains constant

blocks.prompt: 57 Why does the Earth's axis of rotation stay fixed in one direction in space?
blocks.explanation: Angular momentum is a vector along the axis, and the axis does not change orientation unless an external torque acts. The major force on the Earth is the pull of the Sun, which gives no sizeable torque, so the axis stays fixed.

book_ref.quote: The Earth's axis of rotation, therefore, remains fixed in one direction with reference to the universe around us.

blocks.prompt: 58 Why does a bike at rest fall over while a moving bike stays upright?
blocks.explanation: A moving bike's wheels spin and have angular momentum along their axles. This angular momentum resists any tendency to change, which keeps the bike upright and stable. At rest the wheels have no angular momentum.

book_ref.quote: the angular momentum of the spinning wheel resists any tendency to change and helps to keep the bike upright and stable

blocks.prompt: 59 Why does a whirling ball speed up as its string wraps around a finger?
blocks.explanation: No external torque acts, so angular momentum (L = mr²ω) stays constant. As the string wraps, r and hence the moment of inertia decrease, so the angular speed and the ball's speed increase.

book_ref.quote: The ball's speed increases as the string wraps around the finger.

blocks.prompt: 60 How does an ice skater change his rate of spin?
blocks.explanation: Folding the arms and bringing the stretched leg in decreases his moment of inertia, so his angular velocity increases (Iω constant). Stretching hands and a leg outward increases the moment of inertia and the angular velocity decreases.

book_ref.quote: can increase his angular velocity by folding arms and bringing the stretched leg close to the other leg

blocks.prompt: 61 A man on a turntable with outstretched dumb-bells turns at 1.2 rev s⁻¹ with I = 6.0 kg m². He draws his hands in and I becomes 4.0 kg m². Find his new angular speed.
blocks.explanation:
I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂
ω₂ = I₁ω₁/I₂ = 6.0 × 1.2 / 4.0 = 1.8 rev s⁻¹

book_ref.quote: As he draws his hands inward, his angular speed at once increases.

blocks.prompt: 62 Why does the duration of the day increase when polar ice melts and flows away as rivers?
blocks.explanation: The water moves away from the Earth's axis, so the moment of inertia of the Earth increases. Angular momentum is conserved (Iω constant), so the Earth's angular velocity decreases and the day becomes longer.

book_ref.quote: the moment of inertia of water and hence that of Earth about its axis of rotation increases

blocks.prompt: 63 A rotating system with a beaker coasts freely. Why does it slow down as water drips into the beaker?
blocks.explanation: No external torque acts, so Iω stays constant. The dripping water adds mass away from the axis, which increases the moment of inertia; therefore the angular velocity decreases.

book_ref.quote: Why does the coasting rotating system slow down as water drips into the beaker?

blocks.prompt: 64 A planet moves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. Why does its orbital speed increase when it is nearer the Sun?
blocks.explanation: The pull of the Sun gives no sizeable torque on the planet, so its angular momentum L = mvr stays constant. When r decreases near the Sun, v must increase.

book_ref.quote: Its orbital velocity increases automatically. Why?

blocks.prompt: 65 What is a flywheel? Give its uses.
blocks.explanation: A flywheel is a heavy wheel with an axle. It stores rotational energy, smooths out output fluctuations and provides stability in bicycles and other vehicles, industrial machinery, gyroscopes, ships and spacecraft. When it spins, its angular momentum resists changes to its orientation.

book_ref.quote: Flywheel is a mechanical device which consists of a heavy wheel with an axle

blocks.prompt: 66 What is a gyroscope? Why is it difficult to change the orientation of its axis?
blocks.explanation: A gyroscope is a mounted flywheel pivoted in supporting rings, used to maintain orientation. Spinning fast with a large moment of inertia, it has a large angular momentum; changing its direction needs a correspondingly large torque, so its axis keeps its orientation.

book_ref.quote: It consists of a mounted flywheel pivoted in supporting rings
